description: Open protocol for deterministic, offline verification of AI agent authorization — cryptographically signed Capability and ActionEnvelope artifacts verified locally without any network calls at decision time.
agents: Not an agent platform — defines the verification substrate that agent platforms implement
Any agent invoking a tool must present a signed ActionEnvelope against a signed Capability
Verifiers evaluate both artifacts locally using a TrustBundle (no central authority required)
High-risk action mode: challenge nonce binding required before execution
Gateway enforcement pattern: verify artifacts at service boundaries before forwarding requests

pp_fit.feature: PP is the enterprise audit + approval layer above Anchor's verification substrate. Anchor proves the action was within signed scope; PP issues the immutable receipt that the action occurred, routes approval for high-risk actions, and provides centralized audit trails.
actions_needing_receipts: Any action submitted as a signed ActionEnvelope — the Anchor protocol explicitly does not provide an audit receipt layer
High-risk actions with challenge nonce enforcement
pp_fit.integration_complexity: low — Anchor's SDKs (Go, TypeScript, Python, Java) provide local verification; PP wraps the VerificationResult to issue a signed receipt and route to audit/approval pipeline
pp_fit.urgency: low — project is early (1 star, last commit Feb 17), founder unknown
pp_fit.strategic_angle: Anchor solves: 'was this action within cryptographically signed scope?' PP solves: 'did this action occur, who approved it, and where is the immutable proof?' These are adjacent primitives — Anchor handles verification-time; PP handles post-execution receipts and enterprise governance. Potential: PP could publish an Anchor-compatible integration pattern or open a spec discussion on the receipt layer gap.

tech_stack.notes: Deterministic verification — same inputs + trust policy = same output. Machine-readable reason codes for audit pipeline integration. Optional transparency reference linkage. Explicitly no network dependency at verification time.

key_primitives: Capability (signed by issuer, scopes allowed actions)
TrustBundle (local trust material for key resolution)

competitive_overlap.vs_pp: Anchor = pre-execution verification that action is within signed scope. PP = post-execution receipt proving action occurred + approval routing + centralized audit. Non-overlapping primitives.
competitive_overlap.vs_grantex: Grantex = OAuth 2.0-style delegated scoping (JWT grants, pre-auth). Anchor = cryptographic local verification at execution time. Anchor is more primitive than Grantex.
competitive_overlap.vs_oath_protocol: OATH Protocol = human-signed intent attestation (local dev workflow). Anchor = machine-verifiable capability delegation (protocol substrate). Compatible layers.
